# Liquidity Pivot and Banking Update

Report 174 | Published 2025-10-26 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-10-26/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/174.json)

Liquidity turning point and bank resilience.

The updated liquidity pivot was timely: QT ended and reserve-management buying began in December. Banking resilience was supported by subsequent data, but the treatment of undrawn lines as not yet at risk is incorrect. Bitcoin failed to follow the simple bullish liquidity narrative on a disclosed annual sensitivity.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 174-C01

**Tariff costs reach consumers**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | coming months |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US retail prices |
| Source blocks | 20, 21, 23 |
| Thesis family | tariff-consumer-pass-through |

Later retailer data show gradual pass-through by December 2025, supporting the stated direction and lag. The evidence concerns covered goods and cannot be generalized to an identical percentage for all CPI.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: coming months

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Gradual tariff pass-through in 2025](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/the-slow-climb-how-tariffs-gradually-raised-retail-prices-in-2025-20260305.html) | Federal Reserve | 2026-03-05 | Verified in the audit

Five-retailer price data show gradual 2025 pass-through; goods imported from China were 8.5% higher year over year in December, with at least 30% tariff pass-through April-December. Coverage is not all consumer spending.

The Fed ended runoff and began reserve-management purchases to preserve ample reserves. This supports the diagnosis of approaching reserve constraints, rather than a claim that all banks were insolvent.

The cited research supports a 12-13% approximate satiation region but explicitly allows demand shifts. It is not a fixed Fed target, and bank cash may include items beyond reserve balances. Distribution and market prices remain necessary.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Time-varying reserve demand curve](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/staff_reports/sr1019.html) | New York Fed | Verified in the audit

Study estimates reserve satiation above 12-13% of bank assets using 2010-24 data. Reserve demand shifts over time; the estimate is not a binding fixed regulatory minimum.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: current/intermediate conditions

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Banking system conditions](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2026-june-supervision-and-regulation-report-report-banking-system-conditions.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2026-06-01 | Verified in the audit

Most banks remained above capital requirements. Large-bank aggregate CET1 was 12% in Q1 2026, with robust liquidity despite reserve declines.
